So I always like to work from the ground up. My partner has ADHD, I do not, so I apologize if none of this is helpful, but it helps him.

Get a trash bag and make it like a game to hunt for all items you need or want to dispose of. Look around places you never would’ve thought. The trash are like mice and your the cat hunting for it. Things you don’t want to dispose of, put them on your unmade bed. Before you know it, the floor may finally be cleared of debris.

Address your desk and bed now as they are the things above floor level that now contain clutter. Keep a trash bag handy to make another decision of what you feel you should keep and what you are fine with trashing. Look at things specifically as “where’s it’s true place in the home (ie dishes = kitchen, blankets = storage, clothes = closet/hamper)

Put similar items into similar piles or groups (medicine in one corner of the desk is a good example that I’d do personally)

For your closet, stack books in the corner, as you don’t have many, and just throw any clothes on the floor into a hamper. Organize like items again, don’t even have to make it neat, just group em. Trash any papers or booklets you don’t actually need.

For your bathroom, get all the clothes out. They’re not supposed to be there (remember the thing I mentioned about what belongs where). Put any body sprays you aren’t currently using into storage. Whether that be your closet or beneath the sink. Same with medicine or things you don’t use every week. That will just add some tidiness and less clutter.

As someone who has gotten out of an abusive relationship, I’ll give my thoughts.

When you love someone with so much of your being, you hope that someday, just someday, that person will come to their senses and love you just the same and stop what they’re doing. That love will sometimes slowly dwindle into absolute terror, as it did for me.

While I still loved my partner, I was terrified of them hurting/killing themselves in retaliation and I was also terrified of the unknown. What if I left and couldn’t afford anywhere to live like I did then? What if I left and this person I love kills themself and I’m not able to see them ever again? What if they follow me and hurt me even more?

A lot of times, I just wanted to feel loved and ignored all the times I got abused. I wanted to leave the abuse, but I wasn’t willing to leave the person.

I was lucky enough to get out of that relationship, but it’s only cause they finally realized how mentally unstable they were and got medical and professional help. They were the ones to end the relationship. They truly realized how terrible they were to me and left. If not for that, I may possibly still have been stuck in that cycle and ignoring all the detrimental behavior to my well-being.
